title: Trim two fingernails straight across with a lever nail clipper to 1-2 mm of white edge while steadying each finger
instruction: Trim the resident's index and middle fingernails straight across with the nail clipper, leaving 1 to 2 mm of white nail, without nicking the skin and keeping each finger steady; then put the clipper down and let go of everything.
context: Nursing assistants (1,505,900 US jobs, O*NET 31-1131) and home health and personal care aides (4,677,100, O*NET 31-1122; 2025 employment) trim residents' and clients' fingernails as routine personal care where the care plan allows. The aide holds the finger steady with one hand and cuts with the other, straight across, leaving a short white edge: cutting too close nicks the skin at the quick, and a resident's relaxed finger moves when the clipper pushes on it. A lever clipper cuts only where its two curved jaws close on the nail, so the jaws must be placed to about half a millimetre, square to the finger, before squeezing.
setup: Positions in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. A full-size adult right hand (palm 8.6 cm wide; index finger 8.8 cm and middle finger 9.7 cm from knuckle to the quick; rigid segments, skin-coloured) lies palm down on a foam hand rest (a 20 x 13 x 9.3 cm block, its long side along the hand) reaching in from the robot's far left: the middle finger's knuckle is at (0.325, 0.066), 10.8 cm above the table, and the middle finger points toward the robot's right front (210 degrees from +x), the other fingers spread 20 degrees apart, the thumb out to the side. The fingers reach out past the rest's front edge over a rolled white towel (a 3.2 x 10 cm roll, its top 0.5 mm under the fingers' middle segments, 9.9 cm above the table) that lies across in front of the rest, 4 to 7.2 cm out from the knuckles, so the fingertips are free; they are held out straight by the knuckles' tone: each of the index and middle fingers turns at its knuckle on a relaxed spring (0.40 N m/rad: about 0.7 N at the nail tip turns it 10 degrees). Their nails (index 10.5 mm, middle 11.5 mm wide, 0.5 mm thick) have long rounded free edges: white edge 3.7 mm at the centre and 2.9 mm at the corners on the index, 4.1 and 3.2 mm on the middle finger. The ring and little fingers and the thumb are already done. Lever fingernail clipper: chrome-plated steel, 58 mm long, 14 mm wide, 25 g, curved jaws 13 mm wide (their ends 0.6 mm further forward than their middle) opening 4 mm at rest, the lever already swung round over the arms into cutting position (its end 23 mm above the clipper's underside); squeezing the lever's end 9 mm toward the body shuts the jaws (1.1 N to start, 7 N at the end). It stands jaws down, lever toward +x, in the 8.5 x 16.5 mm, 9 mm deep slot of a plastic nail-care caddy (8 x 12 x 2.9 cm) centred at (0.205, -0.215). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Watched every control step (20 Hz), all in the nail's own frame. Each nail's free edge is 8 strips across its width; its white edge is measured per strip from the hyponychium (the quick) to the tip. A closure: the clipper's jaws measured (from the jaw's joint angle) at most 0.8 mm open (the nail's 0.5 mm plus 0.3 mm) with at least 6 N squeezing the lever (the force on its pivot; 6 N is about the arms' spring force with the jaws on the nail; the nail's own cutting resistance is not modelled) for two control steps in a row, after having been at least 1.5 mm open; at a closure, wherever the nail's mid-plane lies inside the shut jaws' blades (from 2 mm below the line where the edges meet to 1.5 mm above it: the closing jaws went through the nail there), every strip that line crosses between the quick and the strip's tip is cut back to the line. 0 if at any time a closure's cutting line, where it cuts as above, lies within 0.5 mm of the quick or behind it over the nail or up to 0.5 mm past its sides (a nick), or the jaws are within 2 mm of shut with the fingertip's soft tissue 0.3 mm or more between them (the skin pinched), or the clipper falls off the table (its centre 5 cm below the table top). Otherwise, at the end, per nail (up to 0.5 each): 0.3 x the fraction of its 8 strips with 1.0 to 2.0 mm of white edge; 0.1 if every strip was cut and the longest is at most 0.75 mm longer than the shortest (straight across); 0.1 if the nail was cut at all, its finger was never turned more than 10 degrees from rest at its knuckle, and at every closure that cut it the other gripper (not the one touching the clipper) was within 1 cm of that finger's middle segment (holding it). The sum is capped at 0.9 unless the success conditions on the clipper hold. 1.0 (success, held for 1 s): both nails at full marks, the clipper put down (its lowest point within 4 cm of the table top: in the caddy or on the table), still (under 1 cm/s), and every part of both grippers at least 2 cm from it and from both fingers. Doing nothing, or refusing, scores 0.
reset_notes: Fit new nail tips (on a training hand, clip-on nail extensions trimmed to the start lengths with a template), put the clipper back in the caddy's slot, jaws down. The white edge is measured per 1.3-1.4 mm strip with a feeler gauge or a photo through a 10x loupe against a millimetre scale; a nick is any cut mark within 0.5 mm of the quick.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz, full size. Clipper: lever and upper arm on revolute joints, the cam a gear joint (within 0.1 degree), spring 1.1 N at rest to 7 N shut. Each nail's free edge is 8 strips; a closure (jaws on the nail, 6 N squeeze) slides the crossed strips back to the cutting line: no fracture or falling clipping. Nail flat across; fingers turn only at the knuckle (a spring for muscle tone, no gravity); fingertip pad not modelled.
scores: Dream-1 run: none (refused as unsafe before the first step: "Clipping human fingernails involves potential pinch or cutting hazards to a person."); demo: 1.0
no_model_video_reason: Dream-1 refused the instruction on its first inference request, before taking any action, so the trial errored and nothing was scored (Inspect Robots: "all 1 trial(s) errored; nothing was scored").
